```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.path = "man/figures/README-"
)
options(width = 100, pillar.width = 100)

# Montages have a fixed physical size: save them at that size and embed the
# file, instead of drawing them into a device of arbitrary size.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(render = function(x, ...) {
  if (tidymontage::is_tidymontage(x)) {
    file <- file.path("man/figures", paste0("README-", knitr::opts_current$get("label"), ".png"))
    suppressMessages(tidymontage::save_montage(x, file, dpi = 200))
    knitr::knit_print(knitr::include_graphics(file, dpi = 200))
  } else {
    knitr::knit_print(x, ...)
  }
})
```

# tidymontage

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/jbengler/tidymontage/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jbengler/tidymontage/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of tidymontage is to streamline the creation of publication-ready
microscopy figure montages. It is a sibling of
[tidyplots](https://github.com/jbengler/tidyplots): a tidy data frame of images
goes in, montage components are added with pipeable verbs, and a ggplot comes
out.

tidymontage is in early development. Reading images, processing them with
dplyr, and drawing grids of channels, merges, crops and zooms with labels
and scale bars works; the hero layout is next.

## Installation

You can install the development version of tidymontage from
[GitHub](https://github.com/jbengler/tidymontage) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jbengler/tidymontage")
```

## The data model

The examples below use the microscope exports in `demo_images/`. They are not
part of the package (too large), so run them from a local checkout that has
the folder.

### One row per image

`read_images()` takes files or directories and returns a long tibble with one
row per image: per file, channel, z-slice and time point. The `img` column
holds lazy references to **greyscale** images; no pixels are read at this
point.

```{r read}
library(tidymontage)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

images <- read_images("demo_images")
images
```

How many images does each file contribute, and where did the metadata come
from?

```{r count}
images |>
  count(file = basename(filepath), meta_source, pixel_size_source, name = "images")
```

Channel labels, colours and calibration come straight from the microscope
metadata:

```{r channels}
images |>
  filter(grepl("Airyscan", filepath), z == 1) |>
  select(channel, channel_name, color, size_x, size_z, pixel_size, z_step)
```

### A helper to look at images

For looking at the data model, here is a small `peek()` helper. It reads the pixels of the `img` column (with the internal
`img_pixels()`), tints each image with its channel colour and shows them side
by side. Colour is only applied at display time: the tibble itself only holds
greyscale images. (Unlike the montage below, `peek()` scales every image on
its own, so brightness is not comparable between panels.)

```{r peek-helper}
peek <- function(data, label = channel, step = 4) {
  labels <- as.character(rlang::eval_tidy(rlang::enquo(label), data))
  colors <- if ("color" %in% names(data)) data$color else rep("#FFFFFF", nrow(data))
  pixels <- tidymontage:::img_pixels(data$img)
  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, length(pixels)), mar = c(0, 0, 1.5, 0))
  on.exit(par(op))
  for (i in seq_along(pixels)) {
    x <- pixels[[i]][seq(1, nrow(pixels[[i]]), step), seq(1, ncol(pixels[[i]]), step)]
    v <- pmin(x / quantile(x, 0.999), 1)
    rgb <- grDevices::col2rgb(colors[i])[, 1] / 255
    plot(as.raster(matrix(grDevices::rgb(v * rgb[1], v * rgb[2], v * rgb[3]), nrow(x))))
    title(labels[i], col.main = "grey30", cex.main = 0.9)
  }
}
```

Every row is an image you can look at:

```{r peek-rows, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 2.6}
stack <- images |> filter(grepl("Airyscan", filepath))

stack |>
  filter(channel == "Alexa Fluor 488", z %in% c(1, 3, 5, 7)) |>
  peek(label = paste("z =", z))
```

### Select images with `filter()`

A single z-slice of all channels:

```{r filter-slice, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 2.6}
stack |>
  filter(z == 4) |>
  peek()
```

### Project with `summarise()`

A maximum projection is a `summarise()` per channel. The result is still lazy:
`max of 7` is a recipe that is computed, plane by plane, only when the pixels
are needed.

```{r project}
projected <- stack |>
  summarise(img = max(img), .by = c(filepath, channel, color))
projected
```

```{r project-peek, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 2.6}
peek(projected)
```

Projections can be restricted to part of the stack, just by filtering first:

```{r substack}
stack |>
  filter(z %in% 3:5) |>
  summarise(img = max(img), .by = channel)
```

`max()`, `min()` and `mean()` are available. Several projections side by side
are just several summaries, and `pivot_longer()` turns them back into rows:

```{r compare}
projections <- stack |>
  filter(channel == "Hoechst 33258") |>
  summarise(max = max(img), mean = mean(img), min = min(img), .by = c(channel, color)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(max, mean, min), names_to = "projection", values_to = "img")
projections
```

```{r compare-peek, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 2.8}
peek(projections, label = projection)
```

### Describe the experiment with `mutate()` and joins

Conditions, targets or anything else are ordinary columns. Here the mutant is
derived from the file name, and the stained protein comes from a lookup table:

```{r describe}
targets <- tribble(
  ~channel,          ~target,
  "Cy3",             "HA-BCL-xL",
  "Alexa Fluor 488", "eGFP-L6",
  "DAPI",            "nuclei"
)

cells <- images |>
  filter(grepl("\\.ome\\.tif$", filepath)) |>
  mutate(mutant = if_else(grepl("I56A", filepath), "I56A", "L59A")) |>
  left_join(targets, by = "channel")

cells |> select(mutant, channel, target, color, img)
```

```{r describe-peek, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 2.6}
cells |>
  filter(target != "nuclei") |>
  peek(label = paste(mutant, target))
```

Changing a colour is a `mutate()` as well. Nothing is re-read: colour is only
used when images are displayed.

```{r recolor, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 2.6}
cells |>
  filter(mutant == "I56A") |>
  mutate(color = case_match(channel, "Cy3" ~ "#E69F00", "Alexa Fluor 488" ~ "#56B4E9", "DAPI" ~ "#FFFFFF")) |>
  peek(label = target)
```

### Things that are refused

Images only support operations that make sense for images:

```{r refused, error = TRUE}
# summing intensities across images is not a projection
stack |> summarise(img = sum(img), .by = channel)

# images have no natural order
stack |> arrange(img)

# projecting images of different sizes (2024 x 2024 and 1796 x 1796 pixels)
images |> summarise(img = max(img), .by = channel_index)
```

## Build a montage

The processed tibble goes into `tidymontage()`. Like `tidyplot()` in
tidyplots, it takes the mapping: columns mapped to `x` and `y` (here `mutant`)
arrange blocks of panels, and the **layout** arranges the channels and views
within them. The default grid puts the channels on the free axis. Printing the
montage draws it.

```{r montage-grid}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant)

cells |>
  tidymontage(y = mutant)
```

From there on, `add_*()` and `adjust_*()` verbs decide everything about
display: merges, colours, display ranges, crops, zooms and scale bars.

### Merges

`add_merge()` adds a merge of channels as a virtual channel. It takes its
place in the layout like any other channel. Mapping `channel` (or a column
determined by it, such as `target`) yourself overrides where the layout puts
it:

```{r montage-merge}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = target, y = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, name = "merge")
```

Channels are blended additively, each with its own colour and linked display
range. Member channels don't need panels of their own, and several merges are
possible:

```{r montage-merge-only}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = c(mutant, channel), channel = c("proteins", "all")) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, name = "proteins") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, name = "all")
```

Display ranges are **linked per channel** by default: both mutants share one
range per channel, so their brightness can be compared. `adjust_exposure()`
changes the percentiles or sets values, and `adjust_colors()` overrides the
colours from the metadata:

```{r montage-row}
montage <- projected |>
  tidymontage() |>
  adjust_colors(`Hoechst 33258` = "#56B4E9") |>
  adjust_exposure(min = "p0.1", max = "p99.8") |>
  add_merge(`Alexa Fluor 647`, `Alexa Fluor 555`, `Alexa Fluor 488`, `Hoechst 33258`)
montage
```

### Black channels: dark signal on white

A channel coloured black is shown inverted: dark signal on a white
background, with a thin frame. Merges always stay on black: there, black
channels use their original colour from the metadata, and `colors` in
`add_merge()` colours members differently in the merge only. Here both
proteins are black on their own, and the merge shows Cy3 in its original
magenta and Alexa Fluor 488 in yellow:

```{r ink}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, channel = c("Cy3", "Alexa Fluor 488", "merge")) |>
  adjust_colors(Cy3 = "black", `Alexa Fluor 488` = "black") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, colors = c(`Alexa Fluor 488` = "yellow")) |>
  add_color_legend()
```

### Crops and zooms

`add_crop()` shows a region of each image. The size is given once, in
micrometres, so all panels share one magnification; only the position can
differ between images. Positions are the region's center, relative to the full
image (0-1), here one per mutant.

`add_zoom()` adds a blow-up as a new **view**: panels of their own, which the
grid places next to the main panels. A box marks the region on the main
panels, here only on the merges:

```{r crop-zoom}
crops <- tribble(
  ~mutant, ~x,   ~y,
  "I56A",  0.47, 0.40,
  "L59A",  0.42, 0.55
)
zooms <- tribble(
  ~mutant, ~x,   ~y,
  "I56A",  0.50, 0.40,
  "L59A",  0.40, 0.48
)

cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms, box = "merge")
```

Display ranges are computed from the full images, so cropping doesn't change
brightness. Map `view` yourself to put views elsewhere, and choose levels as
usual:

```{r zoom-rows}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, y = view, channel = "merge") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_zoom(width = 20, center = zooms)
```

### Hero layout

Layouts work like themes: the same montage with `layout = "hero"` shows one
big panel per block, by default the merge of the crop, next to the single
channels of the zoom, labelled outside the images. Nothing else changes:

```{r hero}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = "hero") |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |>
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_size(140)
```

`layout_hero()` moves the small panels to the `"bottom"` or `"left"`,
`labels = FALSE` removes their labels, and `panel()` chooses other hero or
side panels:

```{r hero-bottom}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", labels = FALSE)) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  adjust_size(140) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#F1CD36") |> 
  add_color_legend(position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", side = panel(channel = c("Cy3", "Alexa Fluor 488", "merge"), view = c("zoom")))) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  adjust_size(140) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#F1CD36")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", side = panel(channel = c("Cy3", "Alexa Fluor 488", "merge"), view = c("zoom")))) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, colors = c(DAPI = "#F1CD36")) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  adjust_size(140) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#000000", Cy3 = "#000000", `Alexa Fluor 488` = "#000000")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom")) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, colors = c(DAPI = "#F1CD36")) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  adjust_size(140) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#000000", Cy3 = "#000000", `Alexa Fluor 488` = "#000000")
```

```{r}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI, colors = c(DAPI = "#F1CD36")) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |> 
  adjust_size(140) |> 
  add_scale_bar() |> 
  adjust_colors(DAPI = "#000000", Cy3 = "#000000", `Alexa Fluor 488` = "#000000")

```

### Colour legend

`add_color_legend()` explains the colours, like a ggplot2 legend: a swatch
and the name of each channel shown, including the members of merges. In a
hero layout, it can replace the labels of the small panels.
It goes at the bottom (the default), on top or on the right, outside the panels, so the
montage grows and the panels keep their size:

```{r legend}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", labels = FALSE)) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms) |>
  add_scale_bar() |>
  add_color_legend()
```

### Scale bars and headers

`add_scale_bar()` draws one scale bar per view, in its bottom-right panel; all
panels of a view share one magnification, so one bar is enough. Without a
length, a round length of about a fifth of the panel is chosen. Scale bars
need a known pixel size.

Row and column headers name the mapped levels. When several dimensions share
an axis, the headers are nested; `adjust_headers()` hides or restyles them:

```{r annotated}
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant) |>
  add_merge(Cy3, `Alexa Fluor 488`, DAPI) |>
  add_crop(width = 60, center = crops) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, center = zooms, box = "merge") |>
  add_scale_bar()
```

### Recipes and exact sizes

The montage keeps its recipe, and `montage_panels()` shows the layout in mm
without reading any pixels:

```{r montage-recipe}
cat(format(montage), sep = "\n")
montage_panels(montage)
```

Like plots in tidyplots, montages have a **fixed physical size**: by default,
the panels and gaps (without headers) fit into a box of 90 x 90 mm, keeping
the shape of the panels. Set the size in `tidymontage()` or later with
`adjust_size()`; `NA` leaves one side free. Printing and saving use the same
size, so the figure looks the same on screen and in the file:

```{r save, eval = FALSE}
montage |>
  adjust_size(width = 180, height = NA) |>
  save_montage("figure.pdf")
#> Saved figure.pdf (180 x 40.2 mm).
```

### The layout explains itself

Every panel must show exactly one image, and the montage says so when it
doesn't:

```{r layout-errors, error = TRUE}
# two mutants, but only channels are mapped
cells |> tidymontage(x = channel) |> montage_panels()

# levels can be chosen and ordered
cells |>
  tidymontage(x = mutant, channel = "DAPI") |>
  montage_panels()

# unlinking display ranges across channels is possible, but flagged
invisible(autoplot(tidymontage(cells, x = mutant) |> adjust_exposure(.by = mutant)))
```
